title: Nonzero polynomial ideal quotient has a strict dimension bound
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $n\ge1$ be an integer, and put $P=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $I$ be an ideal of $P$ containing a nonzero element and let $R=P/I$ be the quotient ring [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Then $\dim R\le n-1$, where dimension is ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The ideal $I=P$ is allowed, with $\dim(0)=-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), proof, final nonzero residue-polynomial kernel inference: polynomial-source dimension and the strict dimension drop for its nonzero ideal quotient; old item steps 2 and 4.

proof.text: Every nonzero ideal of the field $k$ contains $1$: if $a\ne0$ belongs to it, multiply by $a^{-1}$. Hence its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, both finitely generated, so $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its only prime ideal is $(0)$, and therefore $\dim k=0$ by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Sections 00AR (section-rings-basic) and 00FM (section-Noetherian), Definition 00KE (definition-Krull): direct field specializations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] with coefficient ring $k$ and the finite variable set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Step 1 verifies its Noetherian hypothesis and gives $\dim P=\dim k+n=n$.

source.place: MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_of_isNoetherianRing, lines 118--121; polynomial-source dimension used in Stacks 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), final inference.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne f\in I$. The field $k$ is a domain, so [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain] makes $P$ a domain. Thus $fg=0$ forces $g=0$, which says exactly that $f$ is a nonzerodivisor. By [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], the quotient map $q:P\to R=P/I$ is surjective with kernel $I$, so $q(f)=0$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), proof, final nonzero residue-polynomial kernel inference; basic quotient conventions in section-rings-basic.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-surjective-kernel-nonzerodivisor-dimension-drop] to the commutative rings $P,R$, the surjection $q$, and the nonzerodivisor $f$ killed by $q$. All its hypotheses were checked in step 3. It yields $\dim R+1\le\dim P=n$.

source.place: ringKrullDim_succ_le_of_surjective, lines 60--66; supplies the strict quotient dimension drop implicit in Stacks 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres).

proof.text: If $R=0$, its dimension is $-\infty$, so the assertion holds, including $I=P$. Otherwise [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] puts $\dim R$ in $\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$. Step 4 excludes $\infty$ since $n$ is finite. Writing $\dim R=m\in\mathbf N$, it gives $m+1\le n$, hence $m\le n-1$ since $n\ge1$.

source.place: Definition 00KE (definition-Krull) and Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), proof, last sentence: finite integer form of the strict bound.
